function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (Key Points)** | Topic | Summary | |-------|---------| | **Speed Limits** | • General speed limit on highways: 55–75 mph (varies by county).
• Residential streets: 25 mph (unless posted otherwise).
• School zones: 25 mph during school hours. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on the right. | | **Headlights** | • Must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during rain, fog, or low visibility. | | **Toll Roads** | • Texas has both toll and free interstate segments.
• Toll roads require an electronic toll tag (e‑Tag) or pay‑by‑plate. | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking on sidewalks unless marked. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered annually.
• Most vehicles must pass a safety inspection; emissions testing is required in some counties. | | **School Bus** | • All vehicles must stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle is turning left. | | **Use of Headlights** | • Must use headlights from sunset to sunrise, and during inclement weather. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras are used in many counties; fines are automatically issued. | | **Roadside Assistance** | • Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) provides roadside assistance for registered vehicles. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 5) – full statutory text. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) website – regulations, forms, and updates. - Texas Highway Patrol – enforcement guidelines and public safety notices. **Quick Tips** 1. **Always check local ordinances** – speed limits and parking rules can vary by city or county. 2. **Keep your registration and insurance up to date** – failure to do so can result in fines or vehicle impoundment. 3. **Use hands‑free devices** – cell‑phone laws are strictly enforced. 4. **Be mindful of school zones** – speed limits drop and enforcement is stricter during school hours. If you need more detailed information on a specific law or regulation, let me know!
